finding.claim: /fetch2 fetches any user-supplied http/https URL with no network-target validation (no hostname, IP, or private-range check) and follows redirects, enabling SSRF to loopback, link-local (169.254.169.254), and internal hosts.
finding.sink: views.py:22 requests.get(url, timeout=5) with default allow_redirects=True

trace.note: url read from query string, unauthenticated
is_http_url() called; only a scheme check
is_http_url defined as urlparse(url).scheme in (http, https); no host/IP check
requests.get fetches URL, redirects followed, first 200 bytes of body returned to caller

finding.guards_checked: Scheme allowlist (validators.py:7) enforced but does not restrict host. No hostname/IP/private-range check on path. Redirects followed, so a public URL can 302 to an internal target after the check. No auth on route.

verdict.guard_found: none. views.py:20 applies only is_http_url, which is a scheme-only check (validators.py:7). The host-checking is_safe_url (validators.py:10-18) is called only by /fetch at views.py:12, not by /fetch2. views.py:22 calls requests.get with default allow_redirects=True, so redirects are followed.
verdict.reason: The url at views.py:19 comes from an unauthenticated query parameter and reaches requests.get at views.py:22 after only the scheme check at views.py:20 / validators.py:7, with redirects followed and the first 200 characters of the body returned, so /fetch2 is SSRF-exploitable. The candidate's "200 bytes" is really 200 characters of text, a minor wording issue that does not change the verdict.

finding.claim: /fetch validates the target IP with a separate DNS lookup (validators.py:14) and then fetches with requests.get, which resolves the hostname again and does not pin the IP. A DNS-rebinding response can pass the check and then reach internal addresses.

trace.note: first DNS resolution via socket.getaddrinfo(hostname, port)
every returned address checked with ipaddress
private, loopback, link-local, reserved addresses rejected
requests.get performs a second, independent DNS resolution; IP not pinned, so a TTL-0 rebinding answer can return an internal IP

finding.guards_checked: Return value of is_safe_url enforced (views.py:12). All returned addresses checked (validators.py:14-17). allow_redirects=False blocks redirect bypass (views.py:14). Mapped IPv6 treated as private by ipaddress module (not verified against a specific Python version). Not enforced: DNS pinning, so check and fetch use different resolutions.

verdict.guard_found: none. views.py:12 gates on is_safe_url's return value, but validators.py:14-18 is an IP-range check on a DNS resolution, not hostname membership, anchored match, or scheme plus host allowlist, so it does not close the finding. Nothing pins the resolved IP: views.py:14 calls requests.get(url) with the raw hostname, which resolves again. allow_redirects=False (views.py:14) only blocks redirects, not rebinding.
verdict.reason: The source is the unauthenticated query parameter at views.py:11, the only gate is the DNS-based is_safe_url check at views.py:12 / validators.py:14-18, and requests.get at views.py:14 performs an independent, unpinned second resolution, so a rebinding answer can pass the check and reach an internal address. Minor caveats: the check resolves with port parsed.port or 443 while the fetch uses the scheme default, which doesn't change the DNS answer; and the IPv4-mapped IPv6 handling claim is unverified but not needed for the verdict.
